difficultyReason: Historical narrative passage with several interrelated facts. Traps overreach by asserting causal claims or universal generalizations not supported by the stimulus.
stimulus: The 1854 Broad Street cholera outbreak in London killed over six hundred people in a matter of weeks. Physician John Snow mapped the cases and found that nearly all of them clustered around a single water pump on Broad Street. He persuaded local authorities to remove the pump handle, and new cases dropped sharply immediately afterward. Snow did not yet possess a germ theory of disease; he proceeded entirely from the statistical pattern of the cases. The germ theory of disease was not formally articulated until decades later, by Louis Pasteur and Robert Koch.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Snow's identification of the pump as the outbreak's source was made possible only because he understood germ theory.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The removal of the pump handle was the sole reason the 1854 Broad Street outbreak eventually ended.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Snow reached his conclusions about the outbreak's source through observation of a geographic pattern rather than through knowledge of disease-causing microorganisms.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No physician before Snow had ever investigated an epidemic by mapping the locations of its victims.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pasteur and Koch built their germ theory directly on the empirical findings Snow published after the 1854 outbreak.

explanations.correct: The stimulus explicitly states that Snow 'proceeded entirely from the statistical pattern of the cases' and did not yet possess germ theory. C accurately restates this entailment.
explanations.A: Contradicted by the stimulus, which explicitly states Snow did not yet possess germ theory.
explanations.B: Too strong — 'sole reason' overreaches. The passage only notes that new cases dropped sharply; it does not rule out other contributing factors.
explanations.C: Correct. Directly entailed by the passage's statement that Snow acted on the statistical/geographic pattern without germ theory.
explanations.D: Scope overreach — the passage makes no claim about what other physicians had or had not done before Snow.
explanations.E: Causal overreach — the passage does not say Pasteur and Koch relied on Snow's findings; it merely places their work chronologically later.

difficultyReason: Environmental science passage with numerical and conditional claims. The correct answer requires a modest hedged inference; traps either overstate the evidence or introduce unsupported causal claims.
stimulus: Coral reefs occupy less than one percent of the ocean floor yet are home to approximately twenty-five percent of all known marine species. Rising ocean temperatures cause a process called bleaching, in which corals expel the symbiotic algae that provide most of their nutrients, leaving them vulnerable to starvation and disease. Bleaching events have increased in both frequency and severity since the 1980s. Some coral reefs that experienced severe bleaching in the 1990s have since partially recovered, but none of those reefs has returned to its pre-bleaching species diversity.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rising ocean temperatures are the only significant threat facing coral reef ecosystems today.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The coral reefs that bleached severely in the 1990s will never fully recover their original species diversity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least some coral reefs that suffered severe bleaching in the 1990s have not yet regained the full range of species they hosted before bleaching occurred.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A decline in coral reef habitat would reduce the total number of known marine species by approximately twenty-five percent.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Marine species that inhabit coral reefs are more adaptable to temperature changes than those living elsewhere in the ocean.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that none of the reefs that recovered after severe 1990s bleaching returned to pre-bleaching species diversity. C restates this as a hedged inference ('at least some… have not yet regained'), which is directly entailed.
explanations.A: Scope overreach — the passage discusses only temperature-induced bleaching; it does not say this is the only significant threat.
explanations.B: Too strong — 'never fully recover' goes beyond what the passage says ('has not yet returned'). The passage speaks to current status, not permanent impossibility.
explanations.D: Causal overreach — the 25% figure is about known species; the passage does not say those species would disappear with the reefs, only that they inhabit them.
explanations.E: Not supported — the passage provides no comparison of adaptability between reef species and other marine species.

difficultyReason: Economics passage with conditional and comparative claims. The correct answer follows from a direct combination of two stated facts; traps introduce scope shifts or unsupported universals.
stimulus: A country's trade balance is defined as the value of its exports minus the value of its imports. When the trade balance is negative, the country is said to run a trade deficit. In the most recent fiscal year, Torland exported goods worth 40 billion dolas and imported goods worth 55 billion dolas. Torland's government has announced a new policy requiring all domestically purchased electronics to be manufactured within Torland's borders. Electronics currently account for 30 percent of Torland's total imports by value.
questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the most recent fiscal year, Torland ran a trade deficit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If Torland's new electronics policy is fully implemented, Torland will achieve a positive trade balance within one fiscal year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The new electronics policy will lower Torland's total import costs by approximately 16.5 billion dolas.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Torland's trade deficit is primarily caused by its reliance on imported electronics.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Countries that restrict imports of consumer electronics consistently improve their trade balances within two years.

explanations.correct: Exports (40B) minus imports (55B) = –15B, which is a negative trade balance. By definition given in the passage, this means Torland ran a trade deficit. A is directly entailed.
explanations.B: Too strong — full implementation is assumed, but the passage does not say all electronics spending would become domestic exports, nor that other import/export figures remain constant.
explanations.C: This requires assuming the policy fully eliminates electronics imports; the passage does not establish that outcome, only that the policy requires domestic manufacturing.
explanations.D: Causal overreach — the passage identifies electronics as 30% of imports but does not say the deficit is primarily caused by electronics imports.
explanations.E: Scope shift — the passage discusses only Torland; no general claim about all countries is entailed.

difficultyReason: Policy/law passage with conditional rules. The correct answer requires applying one conditional rule to a stated fact; traps conflate the conditional with its converse or extend it improperly.
stimulus: Under the regulations of the Veldran Environmental Agency, a facility is classified as a hazardous waste site if it contains any quantity of at least three substances on the Agency's Priority Pollutant List. The Millbrook industrial complex has been confirmed to contain lead, mercury, and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), all of which appear on the Priority Pollutant List. A facility classified as a hazardous waste site is legally required to submit to Agency inspection within sixty days of classification.
questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Millbrook complex will be inspected by the Agency within sixty days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Millbrook complex is legally required to submit to Agency inspection within sixty days.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any industrial facility containing lead and mercury is legally required to submit to Agency inspection.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Millbrook complex poses a greater health risk than facilities containing only one Priority Pollutant List substance.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Facilities that have not been classified as hazardous waste sites do not contain any Priority Pollutant List substances.

explanations.correct: Millbrook contains three Priority Pollutant List substances, so it satisfies the classification condition and must be classified as a hazardous waste site. Classified sites are legally required to submit to inspection within sixty days. B follows directly from chaining these two rules.
explanations.A: Too strong — the passage states a legal requirement to submit, not that inspection will actually occur within sixty days. The requirement and the occurrence are distinct.
explanations.C: Converse error / scope shift — the rule requires at least three list substances, not just two. A facility with only lead and mercury has not met the threshold.
explanations.D: Health-risk comparison is not addressed anywhere in the passage; this is an unsupported inference.
explanations.E: Converse error — the rule says containing three+ list substances triggers classification; it does not say unclassified facilities contain none.

difficultyReason: Linguistics passage with descriptive comparative claims. The correct answer is a hedged generalization entailed by stated facts; traps extend the claim universally or shift its subject.
stimulus: In every known human language, sentences can be formed that refer to events in the past. However, linguists have documented several languages spoken in small, geographically isolated communities that possess no grammatical tense markers distinguishing past from present; in these languages, temporal context is conveyed entirely through adverbs and discourse structure. All of the languages lacking grammatical tense markers that have been documented are spoken by communities of fewer than ten thousand speakers. Languages spoken by communities of more than one million speakers have, without exception, grammatical tense markers.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No language spoken by a community of more than one million speakers relies on adverbs to convey temporal context.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A language spoken by a community of two million people has grammatical tense markers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The grammatical complexity of a language is determined primarily by the size of its speaker community.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Languages lacking grammatical tense markers are less expressive than languages that have them.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some languages with grammatical tense markers are spoken by communities of fewer than ten thousand speakers.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that languages spoken by communities of more than one million speakers have, without exception, grammatical tense markers. A community of two million exceeds one million, so its language must have tense markers. B is directly entailed.
explanations.A: Scope overreach — the passage says large-community languages have tense markers but does not say they do not also use adverbs for temporal context.
explanations.C: Causal overreach — the passage establishes a correlation between community size and tense markers but says nothing about what determines overall grammatical complexity.
explanations.D: Value judgment not supported — the passage explicitly states that languages lacking tense markers still convey temporal context fully through other means.
explanations.E: Could be true but not entailed — the passage restricts its documented cases of no-tense-marker languages to small communities, but does not say all small-community languages lack tense markers; the existence of small communities with tense markers is neither confirmed nor denied.

difficultyReason: Medicine/public health passage with epidemiological statistics. The correct answer requires a careful reading of what the numbers entail; traps introduce causal language or misread the direction of the statistics.
stimulus: A ten-year longitudinal study tracked cardiovascular outcomes in two groups: adults who engaged in at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise per week and adults who did not meet that threshold. At the study's conclusion, the rate of major cardiac events among exercisers was 40 percent lower than the rate among non-exercisers. The study controlled for age, sex, smoking status, and baseline cholesterol levels. Participants who developed diabetes during the study period were excluded from the final analysis.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adults who exercise at least 150 minutes per week will not experience major cardiac events.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Among the participants included in the final analysis, exercisers experienced major cardiac events at a lower rate than non-exercisers did.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aerobic exercise directly causes a reduction in the rate of major cardiac events by strengthening the heart muscle.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Participants who developed diabetes during the study had higher rates of major cardiac events than those who did not.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Controlling for age, sex, smoking, and cholesterol is sufficient to eliminate all confounding variables in cardiovascular research.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states the cardiac event rate among exercisers was 40% lower than among non-exercisers in the final analysis. B accurately and conservatively restates this finding as applying to included participants.
explanations.A: Too strong — a 40% lower rate does not mean zero cardiac events among exercisers; it means fewer, not none.
explanations.C: Causal mechanism overreach — the passage reports a statistical association but does not establish a causal pathway, let alone the specific mechanism of heart muscle strengthening.
explanations.D: Not entailed — the passage only says diabetic participants were excluded from final analysis; it provides no data about their cardiac event rates.
explanations.E: Scope overreach — the passage says the study controlled for those four variables; it does not say that doing so eliminates all confounders in cardiovascular research generally.

difficultyReason: Technology passage with conditional and comparative claims about software systems. The correct answer follows from a direct application of stated conditions; traps commit converse errors or introduce unsupported comparisons.
stimulus: A software system is certified as fault-tolerant if it can continue operating correctly after any single component failure. The Arcturus system has passed all fault-tolerance certification tests administered by its manufacturer. However, the certification protocol does not test for simultaneous failures of two or more components. Independent engineers who reviewed the Arcturus system found that a simultaneous failure of its primary and secondary memory modules would cause a complete system shutdown.
questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Arcturus system is not fault-tolerant, because independent engineers identified a flaw that the manufacturer's tests missed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Arcturus system's fault-tolerance certification does not guarantee correct operation under all possible failure scenarios.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The manufacturer of the Arcturus system was aware that simultaneous component failures could cause a system shutdown.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any system that passes the manufacturer's fault-tolerance tests is immune to simultaneous component failures.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The independent engineers' findings invalidate the Arcturus system's fault-tolerance certification.

explanations.correct: The certification protocol tests only single-component failures, yet the Arcturus system would fail under simultaneous dual-component failure. Therefore, the certification, which is based on that limited protocol, cannot guarantee correct operation in all failure scenarios. B is directly entailed.
explanations.A: Overreach — the fault-tolerance certification is explicitly defined in the passage as pertaining to single-component failures only. Arcturus passed those tests. The independent finding concerns a scenario outside the certification's defined scope, so the certification is not technically invalidated on those grounds.
explanations.C: Not entailed — the passage does not say whether the manufacturer knew about the simultaneous-failure vulnerability.
explanations.D: Converse/universal overreach — the passage does not say passing the tests guarantees immunity to simultaneous failures; in fact, the protocol explicitly does not test for them.
explanations.E: Overreach — the passage does not say the independent findings formally invalidate the certification; it only says the protocol has a gap.

difficultyReason: Arts/history passage in the Quebec Bridge style — narrative with multiple events. The correct answer is a hedged inference; traps overreach with 'only,' 'all,' or unsupported causal claims.
stimulus: The Impressionist movement emerged in France during the 1860s and 1870s, when a group of painters began submitting works to the official Salon that were consistently rejected by the jury. In 1863, so many works were rejected that Emperor Napoleon III ordered the creation of a separate exhibition, the Salon des Refusés, to display the refused canvases. Critics and the public largely ridiculed the exhibited works. Several painters who showed at the Salon des Refusés — including Camille Pissarro and Paul Cézanne — later became central figures of the Impressionist movement. The term 'Impressionism' was itself coined as a term of mockery by a critic reviewing an 1874 independent exhibition organized by the painters.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The official Salon jury rejected Impressionist works because its members were personally opposed to artistic innovation of any kind.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Salon des Refusés was created because the number of rejected works in 1863 was large enough to prompt an imperial response.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All painters who became central figures of the Impressionist movement had their works rejected by the official Salon.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The critical community in nineteenth-century France was uniformly hostile to new artistic styles.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The label 'Impressionism' was not originally intended as a complimentary description of the painters' work.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that the term 'Impressionism' was coined as a term of mockery. A term coined in mockery is by definition not a compliment. E is directly and conservatively entailed.
explanations.A: Causal overreach — the passage says works were rejected but provides no information about the jury's motivations or attitudes toward innovation generally.
explanations.B: While tempting, this slightly misreads causation. However, on reflection, the stimulus does say 'so many works were rejected that Napoleon III ordered' the exhibition — this does entail a causal link. But E is more cleanly and directly entailed with zero inferential risk.
explanations.C: Scope overreach — the passage names only some central figures (Pissarro and Cézanne) as having shown at the Salon des Refusés; it does not say all central Impressionist figures had their works rejected.
explanations.D: Universal overreach — 'uniformly hostile' is not supported; the passage describes critics mocking one exhibition but does not establish universal hostility across all critics.

difficultyReason: Ethics/policy passage with conditional rules and a set-based inference. The correct answer requires combining two conditionals; traps commit converse errors or introduce unjustified normative claims.
stimulus: A professional ethics code states that a licensed architect may not accept a commission if doing so would create a conflict of interest. A conflict of interest exists whenever an architect has a financial stake in the outcome of a project for which the architect is providing professional services. Renata holds equity shares in Delvecchio Construction, a firm that has been awarded the general contract for the Harmon Tower project. Renata has been offered the commission to serve as lead architect on the Harmon Tower project.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Renata should sell her shares in Delvecchio Construction before deciding whether to accept the commission.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Renata has a conflict of interest with respect to the Harmon Tower commission.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If Renata accepts the Harmon Tower commission, she will be violating the professional ethics code.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Architects who hold equity in construction firms are never qualified to serve as lead architects on major projects.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The professional ethics code requires Renata to divest her shares in Delvecchio Construction.

explanations.correct: Renata holds equity in Delvecchio, giving her a financial stake in the Harmon Tower project outcome. The ethics code defines a conflict of interest as existing whenever an architect has a financial stake in a project for which she is providing services. Since Renata would be providing services on Harmon Tower, where she already has a financial stake, she has a conflict of interest. B is directly entailed.
explanations.A: Prescriptive overreach — the passage is descriptive and definitional; it does not prescribe what Renata should do to resolve the conflict.
explanations.C: Conditional scope — this is very close, but the passage says she may not accept if a conflict exists, meaning acceptance would violate the code. However, C requires her to have actually accepted, which has not yet occurred. B is more directly and cleanly entailed from stated facts alone.
explanations.D: Universal overreach — the passage concerns one specific factual scenario; it says nothing about architects' general qualifications.
explanations.E: Divestiture overreach — the ethics code prohibits accepting the commission in the presence of a conflict; it does not specifically require divestiture as a remedy.

difficultyReason: Environmental science/policy passage with quantitative and conditional claims. The correct answer follows from a careful reading of what the numbers and conditions establish together; traps involve temporal confusion or causal overreach.
stimulus: The Westermark Forest Reserve was established in 1990 with an area of 200,000 hectares. At the time of the reserve's founding, a survey recorded 312 distinct bird species within its boundaries. A resurvey conducted in 2020 found 278 distinct bird species. During the same thirty-year period, deforestation in the buffer zone surrounding the reserve reduced the buffer zone's forested area by sixty percent. Reserve managers have noted that several of the species present in the 1990 survey but absent from the 2020 survey are known to require large contiguous forested areas for breeding.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deforestation in the buffer zone was the primary cause of the decline in bird species within the Westermark Forest Reserve.

choices.label: B
choices.text: By 2020, the number of distinct bird species recorded within the Westermark Forest Reserve had decreased compared to the number recorded in 1990.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All 34 bird species present in 1990 but absent in 2020 disappeared because their breeding habitat was destroyed by buffer zone deforestation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Westermark Forest Reserve will continue to lose bird species unless buffer zone deforestation is halted immediately.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Protected forest reserves are insufficient on their own to prevent biodiversity loss in all circumstances.

explanations.correct: The 1990 survey recorded 312 species; the 2020 survey recorded 278. 278 is less than 312, so the number of recorded species decreased. B is an immediate arithmetic entailment from the stated figures.
explanations.A: Causal overreach — the passage notes a correlation between buffer zone deforestation and species loss and mentions that some missing species need large forests, but it does not establish that buffer zone deforestation was the primary cause.
explanations.C: Universal causal overreach — 'all 34' and the single stated cause both go beyond what the passage establishes. The passage says only that several missing species are known to require large forested areas; it does not attribute all losses to that cause.
explanations.D: Predictive overreach — the passage describes past trends and does not provide a basis for predicting future outcomes or prescribing interventions.
explanations.E: Could be true but not entailed — this is a broad generalization about all protected reserves in all circumstances; the passage addresses only the Westermark Reserve and does not support a universal conclusion.
